name: Borrowed retained TextLayout row cache

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
# Hypothesis

Borrowing the installed row-layout map during changed-layout preparation removes its full
`HashMap` clone while preserving the existing atomic install and error behavior. Individual
`Arc<WrappedLineLayout>` values remain cloned only when retained by the next installed map.

## Scope lock

This experiment changes only `TextLayoutCache::reusable_rows` and its call site. It does not alter
dirty-row detection, text materialization, row metadata, or prepaint.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
# Measurement plan

Run the focused headed WASM/WebGPU TextArea fixture at both DPRs and inspect its screenshot. Use
source inspection to prove no `HashMap::clone` remains in the reusable-row path, while the
installation remains after successful shaping so an error cannot destroy the prior cache.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
# Expected outcome

The focused TextArea wheel action stays visible and stable. Changed layouts access prior rows by
borrow and only clone each retained `Arc` for the next cache, eliminating the full map clone.

measurements.target: headed WASM WebGPU TextArea wheel action
measurements.note: The unchanged-key scroll path intentionally does not enter reusable-row lookup; this experiment proves a changed-layout allocation reduction by source ownership rather than treating this unrelated wheel timing as a benchmark improvement.

reportMarkdown:
# Borrowed retained TextLayout row cache

The focused Test Suite TextArea page passed headed WASM/WebGPU at DPR 1 and DPR 2, with visible
scroll deltas and nonempty physical-pixel change. `TextLayoutCache::reusable_rows` now returns an
optional borrow of the retained map. `TextLayoutMap` only clones an individual `Arc` when a row is
installed in the new cache; the former whole-map `self.rows.clone()` no longer exists.

The fixed wheel action follows the exact unchanged-key fast path and therefore does not exercise a
changed-layout cache lookup. Its one-sample timings are recorded as runtime health evidence, not as
an allocation benchmark. The reduction is direct from the removed clone and does not alter atomic
error behavior because the installed map remains owned by the cache until successful replacement.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Accept the borrowed reusable-row map. It removes a full allocation and `Arc` cloning pass from
changed-layout preparation without adding state, invalidation rules, or failure paths.
